contradictions.detail: Facebook header states 'Driven 192,000 miles' while the seller's own description says '190k miles maintained with care'. Likely rounding, but the two figures in the same ad do not match and no odometer photo is provided.

KDSS is advertised as a feature and an Ironman kit was installed over it, which is exactly the situation where KDSS leaks and cross-corner lean show up. No photos of the KDSS valve body/accumulators, no lean measurement, no install invoice.

documentation.rationale: Weak on both halves. Identity and terms: no VIN, no odometer photo, no title photo — only a Facebook attribute set (clean title, 2 owners, 192k) and a named private seller with a rating history; the equipment description is detailed and the photos confirm most of it. Maintenance and condition evidence: essentially zero — a bullet list of claimed work (radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters) with no dates, no mileages, no invoices, no scan, no service history, and no documentation of the suspension install. At 192,000 miles the claim list is the least persuasive form of evidence available.

condition.rationale: Photos genuinely look good: straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows with no bolster collapse or cracked dash, working nav/ML/RSE hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws with real tread, tidy rack and hitch. Against that, this is a 192k-mile first-year GX460 with the three expensive model faults — secondary air injection, KDSS, valley-plate/timing-cover coolant seepage — entirely unaddressed in the ad, plus a lift of unknown install quality on a KDSS chassis, and no underhood, undercarriage or cold-start evidence. Trail photos show the car has actually been used off pavement. Unknowns dominate the areas that cost the most.

price_value.rationale: The asking price is far off the market. A 2010 Premium with 173,709 miles is asking $16,995 in Modesto; a 2010 Premium with 230,000 miles sold for $9,800 in Escondido; a 142,900-mile 2010 sold for $14,250 on Cars & Bids; and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same money as this 2010 with 192,000 miles. Bolt-ons (Ironman kit, rack, AT tires, traction boards) recover pennies on the dollar at resale and, per Jason's brief, add modest value at most. The ad has sat nine weeks at one price with no reduction, which is itself market feedback.

mission_fit.rationale: The capability case is real: body-on-frame, low range, locking centre diff, KDSS, Crawl Control, a full-length roof rack that suits a rooftop tent, a hitch, and a third row — all things the RX 350 cannot supply. But this is also a second large Lexus SUV in the driveway, it is a 192k-mile example rather than a low-risk one, and the mission requires it to justify the overlap on capability and dependability. A cheaper, lower-mileage GX would satisfy the same mission with far less exposure.

logistics.rationale: Mission Viejo is roughly 330 miles from Carmel — a one-day drive or a short flight, and Jason will drive a good car home. Southern California means abundant Toyota/Lexus and GX-specialist shops for a PPI including a KDSS-aware inspection, and the seller has a 20-rating marketplace history. Offsets: PPI access is not addressed in the ad, no VIN is published so nothing can be pre-checked, and a California private-party sale requires the seller to supply a current smog certificate, which is unstated.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Grey over beige with wood trim, Mark Levinson, rear entertainment and a tasteful mild overland build is an attractive, coherent package and photographs well on a fire road. It is also an automatic V8 SUV and makes no claim on the enthusiast brief (MINI/GTI/128i/Z3); its appeal is competence and family utility, not character Jason is chasing.

positives: Genuinely capable spec the RX 350 lacks: KDSS, Crawl Control, low range, full-length roof rack suited to a rooftop tent, hitch and a power third row.
Photographic condition is strong for the mileage — straight panels, consistent grey paint, clean beige leather in all three rows, uncracked dash, intact nav/Mark Levinson/RSE hardware.
Southern California car with a matching set of Falken Wildpeak AT3W all-terrains and a level, modest lift rather than a big cheap one.
Toyota 1UR-FE/J150 platform is exactly what Jason's mechanic recommends and parts/specialist support in California is excellent.
Private seller with a long-standing, highly rated marketplace account within a day's drive, so a specialist PPI before money moves is straightforward to arrange.
concerns: Observed: the price is out of step with the comps — $23,995 for a 192,000-mile 2010 when a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 and a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995; it has sat nine weeks with no reduction.
Observed: an Ironman 4x4 lift has been installed over a KDSS chassis with no install invoice, alignment sheet or lean measurement, and the trail photos confirm the truck has been used off pavement.

Observed: every mechanical item is a claim in a bullet list — radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes — with no date, mileage or receipt behind any of it, and no reason given for the radiator and thermostat replacement.
Unverified: secondary air injection status on a 2010-2012 GX460 (ask for a full OBD scan including stored/pending codes, and any P2440/P2442 history or pump replacement invoice).
Unverified: KDSS leak or cross-corner lean (inspect the valve body, accumulators and sway-bar cylinders for weep and measure lean on level ground).
Unverified: 1UR-FE valley-plate and timing-cover coolant seepage, plus frame and underbody condition (request underhood and undercarriage photos and a lift inspection).

seller_questions: What is the VIN, and will you send a photo of the title and current registration?

Who installed the Ironman kit, on what date and at what mileage, and do you have the invoice and post-install alignment printout?
Was KDSS disconnected or re-shimmed during the lift, and can you photograph the KDSS valve body and both sway-bar cylinders for leaks?
Why were the radiator and thermostat replaced — was there a leak or an overheat event — and can you send those receipts with dates and mileage?
Have the transmission, transfer case and front/rear differential fluids been changed, and at what mileage?

What are the DOT date codes on the four Falken tires, and do you have the purchase receipt?

ppi_focus: Secondary air injection: scan for P2440/P2442, check pump operation on cold start and inspect the valves/pump for moisture intrusion.
KDSS: inspect valve body, accumulators and both sway-bar cylinders for hydraulic weep; measure cross-corner lean on level ground and confirm the system still articulates after the lift.
1UR-FE coolant: inspect the valley plate area, timing cover and water pump for seepage; pressure-test the cooling system and check for oil/coolant cross-contamination.
Frame rails, crossmembers and skid areas from below for rust, impact damage or bent components from off-road use.
Lift installation quality: control-arm and shock mounting, CV boot and axle angle, driveshaft/carrier bearing, brake and ABS line routing, and steering geometry/alignment specs.
Transfer case actuator function: shift into 4-Lo and back, confirm no fault codes and no grinding.
Suspension bushings, ball joints, tie rods and rear shocks at 192k miles.
Automatic transmission: fluid condition and level via the check procedure, road-test for shift quality and torque-converter lockup shudder.
Tire DOT date codes and irregular wear pattern that would reveal alignment issues after the lift.
Full body/paint meter check and panel-gap review for unreported collision repair, since no history report exists.
what_would_change_verdict: A clean specialist PPI plus a full scan with no codes, documented healthy KDSS with no lean, and dry valley plate/timing cover — combined with a price renegotiated toward the $15,000-17,000 band the comps support.
Production of dated invoices for the air-injection system, drivetrain fluids and the lift install, converting the claim list into records.
The VIN and a clean history report confirming two owners, no accidents and completed recall work.
Downward: any P2440/P2442 code, visible KDSS hydraulic weep or measurable lean, or coolant seepage at the valley plate — each is four figures on top of an already over-market ask.
Downward: seller declining to release the VIN or to allow a PPI at an independent shop.
evidence.mission_note: This does deliver capability the RX 350 genuinely lacks — body-on-frame, low range, KDSS, roof rack for a rooftop tent, hitch and a third row — so it clears the overlap test on paper. But at 192,000 miles with the three expensive GX460 faults entirely undocumented and an asking price at the level of a 2017 with 64,000 fewer miles, it is not the low-risk capability buy the accelerated_bridge mode calls for at this number.
evidence.rationale: The verdict is driven by price and evidence, not by the truck itself. Condition in the photos is legitimately good: straight grey paint, clean beige leather across three rows, intact Mark Levinson and rear-entertainment hardware, matching Falken AT3Ws and a level, modest lift. But the ad's entire mechanical case is a bullet list — radiator, thermostat, plugs, brakes, filters — with no date, mileage or invoice behind a single line, and at 192,000 miles that is the weakest possible support. Every one of the four model-critical items is missing: no scan for P2440/P2442 secondary air injection, no KDSS leak or lean check on a chassis that has had an Ironman kit installed over it, no underbody or frame images, and no lit-cluster or cold-start evidence. No VIN is published, so no history report, recall check or decode is possible. The market is unambiguous: a 173,709-mile 2010 Premium asks $16,995 in Modesto, a 142,900-mile 2010 sold at $14,250, a 230,000-mile one sold at $9,800, and a 2017 Premium with 128,500 miles asks $23,900 — the same as this. Nine weeks at $23,995 with no reduction confirms the market's read. The build is a modest positive at best under Jason's own rule that accessories never substitute for evidence.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a recent full OBD scan photo (stored and pending codes), the Ironman install invoice with alignment sheet, and confirmation he will meet at a GX/Toyota specialist in Orange County for a lift PPI — and open the price conversation at the $15,000-17,000 the comps support before booking anything.
